title: Per-tenant headroom reconciliation controller and fallback flow for sustained microburst shortfalls
creator: Nadia Cortez
description:
Summary:
Customers on Dedicated reserved pools observed intermittent 5–20s tail latency spikes and request rejections during sustained microburst windows. Root cause analysis shows a combination of three interacting problems: (1) per-tenant warmup credit bookkeeping drifting across AZs, (2) the global autoscaler applying regional cooldown windows that suppressed local replenishment, and (3) the burst-fallback policy preferring model-variant fallbacks before attempting intra-pool headroom rebalancing. Together these produced transient reserved-pool shortfalls despite available physical capacity.

Repro steps and signals observed:
- Repro in staging by replaying customer traffic trace for tenant T-Alpha with 4x short bursts over 10m. We see KV-cache warmup flags not propagating to the lease table (timeline: 2025-02-03 14:12 UTC).
- Metrics: reserved_pool.available_slots decreases while cluster_utilization remains <65% in same AZ.
- Telemetry: warmup_credit_ledger shows negative deltas after concurrent preemptions; headroom_predictor confidence degrades and autoscaler enters suppressed state.
- Logs: scale-controller logs show a cooldown enforcement event (scale-controller/leader.go: cooldown=5m) that blocked a corrective scale-up that would have been per-tenant and low-cost.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Emergency soft-fallback: adjusted routing policy to prefer intra-region fallback (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/traffic-router/pull/1123) which reduced customer error rate by ~80% within 12 minutes.
- Hotpatch: disabled global cooldown enforcement for reserved-pool replenishment (leader toggle rolled for one region) to allow headroom reconciliation runs to proceed (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scale-controller/pull/2337).
- Manual backfill: run one-time credit_reconcile job to repair warmup_credit_ledger for affected tenants.

Proposed long-term fix (this ticket):
1) Implement a per-tenant headroom reconciliation controller that:
   - periodically inspects tenant headroom vs expected warmup_credit ledger,
   - performs corrective lightweight reservations within the same AZ before global scale decisions, and
   - emits a SafetyEvent when local headroom divergence exceeds threshold.
2) Split cooldown windows into "global" vs "local" categories so that low-risk local replenishment is not suppressed by unrelated regional cooldowns.
3) Rework burst-fallback ordering: try intra-pool reallocation and synthetic warmup (short- lived reserve grants) before model-variant fallback for latency-sensitive tenants.
4) Add a reconciliation job that runs hourly to reconcile the warmup_credit_ledger with slot allocation and to surface mismatches in telemetry.
5) Add unit + e2e harness that simulates AZ-specific preemptions and multi-tenant microbursts; integrate into CI so regressions are caught in presubmit.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressively granting synthetic warmup reservations reduces short-term errors but can increase burst accounting complexity and slightly raise cost. We will gate synthetic warmup to labeled low-risk tenants and enable via feature flag.
- Per-tenant controllers add more metadata and leader complexity; we will implement them as low-overhead leader-elect controllers with configurable fanout.

Acceptance criteria:
- No more customer-facing rejections for reproducible staging load within a 6-hour observation window.
- Headroom divergence metric (headroom_divergence_ratio) < 0.05 across tenants during burst tests.
- Controller changes behind a feature flag with telemetry exposing corrective events.
